metadata.note: The Durham and Southern ran 56.8 mi from Durham (Union Station) south through Apex, Holly Springs, Fuquay-Varina and Angier to the Atlantic Coast Line at Dunn, NC. Its southern 36 mi began as the Cape Fear and Northern Railway (Apex - Angier, building from 1898; Angier - Dunn open by 1903), which became the D&S in 1906 - by rename or by successor incorporation, sources differ. Drawn: the CF&N Apex - Angier as a 1900 [ANCHOR] in its own colour, and the D&S Durham - Dunn 1906-1942 [OPEN]. Rule 4: CF&N and D&S are kept as different company strings because the report leaves unresolved whether they were one corporation; if a source shows a simple rename, the CF&N feature should take the D&S colour.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 issue, Durham and Southern entry and index (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt)

metadata.not_yet_sourced: (1) [OPEN] Durham and Southern: Durham - Dunn is drawn to 1942, the last confirmed passenger year; the real end lies somewhere in 1942-1950 (equipment inference 1942-43; trains gone from the Nov 1950 Guide; freight-only by the Feb 1952 Guide). A 'last mixed train' newspaper item or an NCUC order would settle it. (2) [ANCHOR] Cape Fear and Northern: Apex - Angier drawn for 1900 only (Fowler 1900G); the 1899 and 1901 Dunn Democratic Banner pages (DigitalNC) and a 1902-1905 Guide could widen it to c.1899-1906. (3) D&S start: 1906 (annual report) vs 1903 (durhamsouthern.com narrative) vs 1904 (Prince). (4) CF&N -> D&S: rename or new company? Decides whether the CF&N feature shares the D&S colour. (5) Holly Springs depot and the Apex - Holly Springs alignment are not located; 8 mi there are straight lines. (6) Whether D&S trains used the Southern/NCRR main into Durham Union Station and ran into the ACL depot at Dunn. All headways and speeds are estimates.
metadata.omitted: Cape Fear and Northern Angier - Dunn (report block [2], drawable NONE: no source shows CF&N passenger trains south of Angier before 1906). The Erwin spur (Erwin Junction - Erwin, ~2 mi; Fowler lists Erwin with no date letter). The 20 May 1960 detour of SAL No. 21 over Durham - Apex (a Seaboard train on one day, after D&S passenger service had ended).

properties.geometry_quality: Apex - Angier: traced 19.1 mi against a documented ~19.7 mi (D&S mileposts Apex 20.7 to Angier 40.4) and 'twenty miles' (1901 Dunn newspaper, snippet only) - about 3% short. This is the same geometry as the corresponding stretch of the Durham and Southern feature (CF&N track became the D&S south of Apex). Approximated (straight-line) legs, 9.3 mi in all: (1) Apex (south end of the CSX 'D&S Spur', OSM way 346005403, at the SAL crossing) - Holly Springs, 5.8 mi; (2) Holly Springs - north end of the mapped grade (OSM way 1437034297, about 2 mi south of town), 2.2 mi. Neither OSM (rail, abandoned, rail-trail) nor OpenHistoricalMap has anything on this stretch, and the Holly Springs point is the town's Nominatim centroid, NOT a located depot, so these two legs are a guess at the corridor, not its line; (3) 1.0 km (0.6 mi) gap in the mapped grade west of Varina between OSM ways 1437034297 and 1437049183; (4) 0.48 km (0.3 mi) gap east of Fuquay-Varina between ways 1437049175 and 1481060119; (5) 0.57 km (0.4 mi) gap at the north edge of Angier between ways 1481060119 and 16595917. So 9.3 of the 19.1 mi (49%) are straight-line approximation. ERA CAVEAT: drawn on the grade as OSM maps it after abandonment; the 1900 CF&N alignment (described as 'little more than a tramway') may have differed from the later D&S line, and the CF&N's own Apex terminal arrangement is not known.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] Single proven year. The Cape Fear and Northern (B. N. Duke interests; construction began 27 Jul 1898) ran from the Seaboard Air Line at Apex south through Holly Springs and Varina to Angier. The only dated passenger evidence is Fowler's NC file, table 93, which lists two CF&N stations, Blanchard (32.4) and Holland (35.6), as '1900G' - named in the 1900 Official Guide. Service certainly ran wider both ways (a Dunn newspaper of 6 Sep 1899, seen only as a search snippet, mentions passenger traffic on the new road; the company became the Durham and Southern in 1906) but no other year is confirmed: do NOT widen this anchor or bridge 1901-1905 to the 1906 start of the Durham and Southern feature without a timetable or a read newspaper page. The CF&N's extension Angier - Dunn (open by 1903) is NOT drawn: no source shows CF&N passenger trains south of Angier. headway_min 1440 (one train a day) is a placeholder ESTIMATE; frequency is not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: 1900 from Fowler, North Carolina railroads file table 93 ('Blanchard ... 1900G', 'Holland ... 1900G'), as read in research/branches/durham_and_southern_railway.txt (2026-11-05); the tracer did not open the PDF. Headway not sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Durham - Dunn: traced 56.3 mi against a documented 56.8 mi (D&S Timetable #20, 1959, and Fowler table 93) - 0.9% short. Traced chainage vs D&S mileposts: East Durham junction 1.9/2.3, Genlee 9.5/10.4, Carpenter 13.5/14.2, Apex 20.1/20.7, Holly Springs 25.9/26.9, Varina (NS crossing) 32.4/33.4, Kennebec 37.4/38.2, Angier 39.2/40.4, Barclaysville 43.3/44.5, Coats 48.0/48.8, Turlington 51.1/51.8, Erwin Junction 52.7/53.4, Dunn 56.3/56.8. By source: 44.4 mi on ways tagged Durham and Southern, 1.8 mi on the NCRR/Southern main (NS Danville District H Line) from the Durham Union Station site to the junction at East Durham, 9.3 mi straight, 0.2 mi short connectors. Approximated (straight-line) legs, 9.3 mi in all, every one inside Apex - Angier: (1) Apex (south end of the CSX 'D&S Spur', OSM way 346005403, at the SAL crossing) - Holly Springs, 5.8 mi; (2) Holly Springs - north end of the mapped grade (OSM way 1437034297, about 2 mi south of town), 2.2 mi. Neither OSM (rail, abandoned, rail-trail) nor OpenHistoricalMap has anything on this stretch, and the Holly Springs point is the town's Nominatim centroid, NOT a located depot, so these two legs are a guess at the corridor, not its line; (3) 1.0 km (0.6 mi) gap in the mapped grade west of Varina between OSM ways 1437034297 and 1437049183; (4) 0.48 km (0.3 mi) gap east of Fuquay-Varina between ways 1437049175 and 1481060119; (5) 0.57 km (0.4 mi) gap at the north edge of Angier between ways 1481060119 and 16595917. DURHAM END: Union Station (1905-1968) is approximated as the NCRR main at Corcoran St, downtown; the 1.8 mi into it is drawn on the Southern/NCRR main, on the assumption (not sourced) that D&S trains reached the station over it rather than over a D&S track of their own. DUNN END: the line stops at the D&S junction with the Atlantic Coast Line (CSX South End Subdivision) on the north side of Dunn; whether D&S trains ran on into the ACL depot is not known and that last half mile is not drawn. ERA CAVEAT: Durham - Apex is drawn on the alignment of today's CSX freight track and Apex - Dunn on the grade as OSM maps it after abandonment (1981 / c.2000); 1906-1942 line changes, if any, were not checked. The Erwin spur (about 2 mi, OSM ways 16595913, 294421091, 371290928) is in OSM but deliberately not drawn - the report finds no dated passenger evidence for it.

segments.note: Durham and Southern passenger service Durham (Union Station) - East Durham - Genlee - Carpenter - Apex - Holly Springs - Fuquay Springs/Varina - Angier - Barclaysville - Coats - Turlington - Erwin Junction - Dunn. START 1906: the D&S 1958 Annual Report (quoted at durhamsouthern.com) says the Durham extension had been 'built and put into operation' by 3 June 1906, and the D&S name is in the 1906 Official Guide (Fowler). Sources conflict - durhamsouthern.com's narrative says the line was complete Durham - Dunn in summer 1903, Prince (as quoted there) 1904 - and the later, firmer date is drawn. SERVICE: passenger trains Nos. 11-12 ran the length of the railroad in the June 1934 Official Guide; by December 1941 they had become mixed trains (Hanson, ACL&SAL Historical Society forum, 2002, from the Guides); a 1941 Angier - Varina ticket survives (Ashworth, same thread); the 1942 Durham Union Station board lists D&S No. 11 (mixed) dep. 4:20 pm for Dunn and No. 12 (mixed) arr. 2:45 pm (chicagorailfan.com). [OPEN] END: passenger service is confirmed to 1942. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when service actually stopped. Ashworth infers 1942-43 from the coach count in the annual reports (several in 1942, one in 1943, none in 1944), but mixed trains may have carried passengers in the caboose; Nov 1950 Guide no longer lists the trains (Hanson); the Feb 1952 Guide index daggers every D&S station 'For freight only'. American-Rails' 'after 1952' is contradicted by that Guide and rejected. Do not extend without evidence. 1930 Duke Power ownership was a stock change, same operator - no split. Freight continued (SCL 1979, CSX Durham - Apex today; Apex - Erwin Jct lifted c.1981; Dunn - Erwin a rail-trail since c.2000) - context only. headway_min 1440 (one round trip a day) is an ESTIMATE from the Nos. 11-12 pattern.
sources: Segment-level: start 1906 from the D&S 1958 Annual Report as quoted at durhamsouthern.com/history.html; 1934 and Dec 1941 Official Guide entries (Hanson) and 1941 ticket (Ashworth) from the greenspun thread; 1942 mixed Nos. 11/12 from chicagorailfan.com; freight-only by the Feb 1952 Official Guide index (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt) -- all as quoted in research/branches/durham_and_southern_railway.txt (2026-11-05); the tracer did not re-open these pages.
